recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中大量具明顯核仁、細緻染色質的大型芽細胞，加上胞質空泡化、核呈兩個分離圓形小葉的小型發育不良巨核細胞（hypolobated/bilobed megakaryocyte），且血小板數正常；染色體核型圖在 3 號染色體 q21 與 q26 處有箭頭標示，指向 inv(3)(q21q26.2) 的急性骨髓性白血病。
features: Aspirate: numerous large blasts with high N:C ratio, round to oval nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin and one to several prominent nucleoli
Blast cytoplasm moderate, pale gray-blue and agranular, without visible Auer rods
Dysplastic megakaryocyte with vacuolated cytoplasm and two separate round nuclear lobes (non-lobated/bilobed form)
Biopsy: hypercellular marrow with sheets of immature cells and scattered small, hypolobated megakaryocytes in loose clusters
Karyotype: arrows at 3q21 and 3q26 on one chromosome 3 homolog, indicating an inversion of chromosome 3
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smears show numerous large blasts with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, finely dispersed chromatin, prominent nucleoli and moderate agranular gray-blue cytoplasm; Auer rods are not identified in the fields shown. Megakaryocytes are dysplastic, including a small form with vacuolated cytoplasm and two widely separated round nuclear lobes. The core biopsy is hypercellular with sheets of immature cells and scattered small hypolobated megakaryocytes, some clustered. The karyogram shows an abnormal chromosome 3 with breakpoints marked at 3q21 and 3q26; only a single X chromosome is displayed and the full karyotype string is not provided in the figure. In a patient with 44% circulating blasts and a preserved platelet count, findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia with inv(3)(q21.3q26.2); GATA2::MECOM.

ddx.vs: Multilineage dysplasia may look identical, but the small hypolobated/bilobed megakaryocytes with normal-to-high platelets and the inv(3)/t(3;3) MECOM rearrangement define this entity and take precedence.

AMKL has blasts with cytoplasmic blebs expressing CD41/CD61 and often marrow fibrosis, whereas here the blasts are nondescript myeloblasts and megakaryocytic abnormality is confined to maturing dysplastic megakaryocytes.
MDS-EB has fewer than 20% marrow and blood blasts, whereas this case shows sheets of blasts and 44% peripheral blasts.
Morphology and cytogenetics can be identical; the distinction rests on a history of cytotoxic therapy, which this patient lacks.
